citations.description: test_materialize_completes_without_lazy_fetch asserts success (all files present), not failure with a descriptive error
_ensure_blobs_present is best-effort and silent on failure; it fetches blobs up front so materialization succeeds rather than failing fast with a descriptive error
Ticket AC1 text: 'materializing a tree whose blobs are absent from a partial clone fails within seconds with a descriptive error naming the remedy'

findings.criterion: AC1: materializing a tree whose blobs are absent from a partial clone fails within seconds with a descriptive error naming the remedy, pinned by a unit test using a --filter=blob:none clone fixture
findings.detail: The implementation does NOT make materialization fail with a descriptive error naming the remedy. Instead, `_ensure_blobs_present` fetches blobs up front in one RPC so that `materialize()` succeeds. The test `test_materialize_completes_without_lazy_fetch` asserts that all 40 files are present and readable after materialization — i.e., it asserts success, not failure. The 'fails within seconds with a descriptive error naming the remedy' sub-requirement is unmet. The fixture and test do use `--filter=blob:none` (the second sub-requirement is met), but the primary behavioral requirement — fail-fast with a descriptive error — is not implemented.
